revisions.claim: As a byproduct of the governed development process, the broad execution-and-learning initiative was split into separately verifiable integration boundaries: a read-only orchestrator, an append-only human review ledger, and a non-applying promotion preview.

ai_tool: generated implementation, records, and tests under review
human: approved, redirected, or stopped each governed boundary

revisions.factuality_note: The repository history verifies the staged split and resulting boundaries. It does not prove that one person independently derived and implemented the complete decomposition without AI assistance.

value_assessment.audience: AI-assisted solo developers, solo founders, collaborators, and small teams
value_assessment.value: The split reduced coupling and made the larger loop testable in bounded stages.

revisions.claim: The repository contains a deterministic, repository-local, read-only governed loop orchestrator produced through AI-assisted development under human-set goals, constraints, acceptance criteria, and approval gates.

human: reviewed failures and approved the bounded result

revisions.factuality_note: The implemented artifact and tests are verified. The wording avoids attributing all architecture and code authorship directly to the human operator.

value_assessment.audience: AI-assisted solo developers, solo founders, collaborators, and small teams
value_assessment.value: The project output provides a reconstructable control loop without unattended execution authority.

revisions.claim: As an integration byproduct of completing the governed loop, one committed loop run links eight deterministic verification stages while retaining read-only authority.

human: accepted the integrated result after CI and review

revisions.factuality_note: The eight-stage linkage is verified in the repository. This record describes the resulting integration artifact rather than claiming sole direct implementation by the human operator.

value_assessment.audience: AI-assisted solo developers, solo founders, collaborators, and small teams
value_assessment.value: The integration byproduct provides a single reconstructable state view across the governed components.

revisions.claim: Independent review of the Adaptive Governance Compiler identified under-governed G0 classification and context-rebinding risks; the AI-assisted development process then incorporated fixes and regression tests accepted through human review.

human: accepted the repaired boundary after tests

revisions.factuality_note: The review findings, fixes, tests, and acceptance are evidenced by the pull request. This is an audit-remediation byproduct, not proof that the human operator personally discovered or coded every correction.

value_assessment.audience: AI-assisted solo developers, solo founders, collaborators, and small teams
value_assessment.value: The remediation shows that external review findings can be converted into enforceable fail-closed checks.

revisions.claim: Across several RTS components, the project repeatedly used exact fingerprints, stale-state checks, CI verification, review remediation, and completion records. This is evidence of a potentially reusable development pattern, not yet proof of reuse outside RTS.

human: repeatedly required reconstruction, review, and completion evidence
decided how to recover after failures

revisions.factuality_note: Repeated use inside RTS is verified. General reusability and reduced failure rates outside this repository remain unverified, so the record is classified as a signal rather than a completed reusable asset.

value_assessment.audience: AI-assisted solo developers, solo founders, collaborators, and small teams
value_assessment.value: The repeated pattern is a candidate for reuse and later validation in other projects.
